Guardian Druid Rotation in 

The Guardian Rotation is one of the most simple and easy to manage in the whole game.
We have only a few short cooldown spells we want to use as often as possible and no real debuffs or procs to track.
The main thing to focus on for Guardian is ensuring you have enough rage to use defensively when you require it.

 

 

 
 Avoid Rage Waste: Rage should be spent intentionally. Unecessary over-use of Ironfur will be a huge DPS loss.
 

 

 
 

 
 Keep Abilities on Cooldown: Making sure you are casting Mangle and Thrash as often as possible ensures the rotation flows smoothly. 
 

 

 
 

 
 Rotate Defensive Cooldowns: Having a defensive cooldown at the right time makes a world of difference as a tank spec. 
 

 

Guardian Druid Starter Guide

 Best Guardian Druid Rotation

Guardian rotation is extremely simple and that fact has always been a massive draw to the spec. It revolves around pressing a couple short cooldown buttons frequently ( Thrash and Mangle ) and then spending rage offensively ( Raze ) or defensively ( Ironfur ).

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Guardian Druid: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.

Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Guardian Druid to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Guardian Druid Major Cooldown Usage

Guardian Druid has a small selection of cooldowns with varying durations and timers. In ideal circumstances, such as when you have a full understanding of the encounter, you should be able to time or hold certain cooldowns to pair with others as they become available again. Do this only if you won't lose any cooldown uses during the encounter. If you don't understand how to time your cooldowns properly, then use them off cooldown when available.

While this buff is active, you want to try to get as many casts of Thrash and Mangle off as possible, while also spending your Rage on Maul , Raze , or Ironfur to avoid capping Rage. 

You should aim to use as many Maul s/ Raze s as possible during the buff window, as it is a large damage boost. It also grants us a considerable health boost and can be one of our better defensive cooldowns.

Pressing Heart of the Wild casts a single spell depending on which form you are in.
For Cat Form this is Feral Frenzy - A large single target DoT.
For Human/No Form it casts Wild Growth - A short HoT for you and your group.
For Boomkin Form it casts Starfall - A buff that lasts 8 seconds that deals low damage to all targets in combat with you slowly.
Generally it is used in Cat Form for the large single target DPS increase but sometimes the group heal can save lives.

A 50% damage reduction on a fairly long cooldown. This is our biggest damage reduction cooldown and should be used sparingly for dangerous periods during a pull or encounter.

An extremely short cooldown that should be used as frequently as possible to smooth overall damage intake. Rarely, you can hold it for a short time to align with bigger damage spikes.

 Guardian Druid Advanced Tips

 
 Spending Rage 

Whether you want to improve surviving or want to improve your damage. Spending rage will be the main focal point of both.
Pressing Ironfur when you don't actually need it defensively is now quite a significant dps loss.
As our goal is to stay above 80 rage with each cast of Maul due to Harnessed Rage , pressing Ironfur drains that rage quickly and stops the cycle of high rage expenditure.
This means we end up filling our GCD's with useless abilities like Swipe which generate no rage and deal very little damage. The more you are swiping the less DPS you are doing efficiently.
Alternatively, not pressing Ironfur when a large physical hit is coming or significant flow of melee swings, can easily lead to death. So finding a comfortable balance between these 2 is integral.

Comment by pj4ever1989 
Hello Pumps,

You write that: " Soulshape The usefulness of this ability is quite average, still requiring us to shift back into bear form afterwards.".

This is technically not true, as your form is retained. You just need to have a macro to cancel Soulshape and you will be back in Bearform without any extra GCD lost (apart from the actual blink). This also works for all other forms.

Example: Be in Bear form, use Soul Shape, use Macro "/cancelaura Soulshape", You are now in Bearform again :).

Cheers, and thanks for the write-up!

It maintains a WoW addon called the Wowhead Looter , which collects data as you play the game! 

 

It uploads the collected data to Wowhead in order to keep the database up-to-date! 

 

 
You can also use it to keep track of your completed quests, recipes, mounts, companion pets, and titles!
